scenario: AITA for not ending my friendship with my best friend after he cheated on my sister? | Both my best friend and my sister know about my other account so this is a throwaway. I'm an 18 year old guy and I have a twin sister. I've been best friends with my best friend (we'll call him G) since kindergarten, so G and my sister have always been pretty close too. They've kind of had a "thing" going on our whole lives. For the longest time, they never officially dated for a bunch of different reasons I won't get into, but they were always really close and really into each other. A little over a year ago, when we were all 17, they finally started dating. Everything went really well for like 13 months, but then long story short, G cheated on my sister and I was the one who figured it out. He swore it wouldn't happen again and begged me not to tell my sister but I told her anyway. I was mad at him and he was mad at me so we didn't talk for a month and a half, which was honestly the weirdest month and a half of my whole life. G's practically like my brother, we've been inseparable since kindergarten, so not having him around was kinda....unbearable honestly lol After our streak of not talking to each other, G invited me on his family ski trip as a way to make amends (I've been on lots of his family's ski trips through the years). I accepted and ended up forgiving him and letting him back into my life because it was way too weird without him in it. I can tell he's genuinely sorry about what happened. He literally cried cause he felt so bad and I've only seen him cry like once before in my whole life Anyway, G and my sister broke up as soon as she found out he cheated and they're still not on speaking terms, so my sister obviously isn't happy about the whole situation. She's making me feel like shit for still being friends with G, and she doesn't seem to understand how big of a deal it would be for us to lose our 13 year friendship over her. I know G made a huge mistake, I hate him for it and I'll never 100% get over it, but I'm not gonna let it ruin my best and longest friendship. I think about it like this: if your best friend cheated on their SO and then felt like shit, would you end your friendship with them? No. So why is this any different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall (a different college in a different state than the one my sister's going to), so none of this is gonna be something that we even think about when we're living in different places Am I the asshole?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole in this situation. Let me start by laying out the facts as I understand them. I'm an 18-year-old guy with a twin sister. My best friend, G, has been like a brother to me since kindergarten. G and my sister have had a close relationship for a long time, and they finally started dating when we were 17. Everything was going well for about a year, but then G cheated on my sister. I found out about the cheating and told my sister, even though G begged me not to. This caused a big fight between G and me, and we didn't talk for a month and a half. It was really weird not having him around because we've been inseparable for so long. After that, G invited me on his family's ski trip to make amends. I went, and after some time, I forgave him and let him back into my life. I can tell he's genuinely sorry because he even cried, which I've only seen once before. G and my sister broke up after she found out about the cheating, and they're still not speaking. My sister is upset with me for still being friends with G and doesn't understand why our 13-year friendship is so important to me. I know G made a huge mistake, and I still hate him for it, but I don't want to lose our friendship over this. I'm thinking that if my best friend cheated on their SO, I wouldn't end our friendship, so why should this be any different just because the SO is my sister? We're both going to the same college in the fall, which is in a different state from where my sister is going. So, maybe this situation won't even come up again once we're there. Now, I'm wondering if I'm being an asshole by not cutting ties with G. My sister is really mad at me, and she's making me feel bad about it. I don't understand why she can't see how important this friendship is to me. I know G messed up, but I'm not willing to lose someone who's been a part of my life since kindergarten. I think about it like this: if it were someone else's sister, would I still feel the same way? Or is it because it's my sister that makes it different? I also wonder if I'm being too lenient with G. Should I hold him accountable for his actions, even if it means losing a friendship? But then again, he's apologized, and he seems genuinely sorry. Maybe giving him another chance is the right thing to do, especially since we're both moving on to college and starting new chapters in our lives. On the other hand, my sister is really hurt, and she's my twin. I don't want to lose her trust or make her feel worse. She's making me feel like I'm not standing up for her, which is important. But I also feel like I'm being asked to choose between my sister and my best friend, which is a tough spot to be in. I'm also considering the long-term implications. If I cut ties with G now, would that affect our relationship forever? Or would it just be a temporary thing? I don't want to look back and regret losing a friendship that's been so important to me. At the same time, I don't want to make my sister feel like I don't care about her feelings. I think about how I would feel if the situation were reversed. If my sister had cheated on someone, would I want G to forgive her? Probably, but that's a different scenario. I guess the key here is that G hurt my sister, and that's a serious issue. But does that mean I have to end our friendship? Or can I still have a relationship with him while acknowledging the mistake he made? I also think about how friendships can survive mistakes. People make mistakes, and sometimes they learn from them. If G is truly sorry and has changed, maybe it's possible to move forward. But I also have to consider my own feelings and whether I can be around him without resentment. Another angle is the impact on my relationship with my sister. If I continue to be friends with G, will that strain my relationship with her? She's already upset, and if I don't take her side, she might feel like I'm not supporting her. But I also don't want to lose G, who has been a significant part of my life. I'm also wondering if there's a middle ground. Maybe I can maintain a friendship with G but set boundaries. For example, not talking about my sister or the cheating incident. Or maybe keeping the friendship but not being as close as before. That way, I'm not completely cutting him off, but I'm also not ignoring my sister's feelings. But then again, setting boundaries might be difficult, especially since G and my sister were so close. It might be hard to have a normal friendship without bringing up past issues. Plus, my sister might not be okay with me even being friends with G, regardless of the boundaries. I'm also considering the advice I've heard from others. Some people say that friendships can recover from mistakes, especially if there's genuine remorse. Others say that betrayals like cheating can have lasting effects and that it's important to prioritize the person who was hurt. In this case, my sister was hurt, and I'm being asked to choose between her and G. I think about how I would feel if I cut ties with G. Would I regret it? Or would I feel better knowing that I stood up for my sister? On the other hand, if I stay friends with G, would I feel like I'm betraying my sister? Or would I feel like I'm making the right choice for myself? I also wonder about the future. If G and I go to the same college, will this situation just fade away as we move on? Or will it continue to be a source of tension between me, G, and my sister? It's possible that time could heal some of these wounds, but I'm not sure. Another thing to consider is whether G has taken responsibility for his actions. He apologized, cried, and seems genuinely sorry. But has he made any changes? Has he done anything to show that he's learned from this mistake? If he's just sorry but hasn't changed, maybe that's a sign that he might repeat the mistake, which would be problematic. But then again, people can change, and maybe G has learned from this experience. It's possible that he's more careful now and won't make the same mistake again. But I can't be sure of that, and that uncertainty might make it harder to trust him again. I'm also thinking about how this affects my own mental health. If I continue to be friends with G, will it cause me stress or anxiety because of the unresolved issues with my sister? Or will it help me move on and have a normal relationship with G? It's a tough balance. In the end, I'm trying to decide whether I'm being an asshole by not cutting ties with G. I know that my sister is hurt, and I don't want to make her feel worse. But I also don't want to lose a friendship that's been so important to me.
